problem: 2 (theology) — the note makes the woman of Canaan an outsider to the chosen seed shown mercy at the edge of the line. The framework reads her as a lost sheep of the divorced northern house living in the land of her exile (the Tyre–Sidon merchant coast), seed revealed by hearing, not a mercy case. The old note had the same error; the rewrite kept it.
quote: The woman of Canaan crying *Son of David* is standing outside that choice, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not pretend otherwise: *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 15:24). Her story matters because he does not erase the line. He keeps it, and still has mercy at the edge of it, where the crumbs fall.
fix: The woman crying *Son of David* on the coast of Tyre and Sidon is not standing outside that choice. Yahusha (Jesus) says *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 15:24) and then heals her daughter, which means she is one of those lost sheep. Canaan was the ground of her exile, the merchant coast where the divorced northern house was swallowed up among the Gentiles (Hosea 8:8), not a verdict on her blood. She knew the Shepherd's voice and called him by David's name because she was a sheep before she ever heard him. The line Jubilees draws is kept; what the story shows is that the chosen seed had been scattered to places their brothers would never have looked.

problem: 2 (theology) — member note carries the same outsider reading.
quote: Not every child of Abraham is the chosen seed; the woman of Canaan stands outside the line the King keeps (Matthew 15:22).
fix: Not every child of Abraham is the chosen seed; the woman on the coast of Canaan who knew the Son of David is one of the lost sheep he was sent to (Matthew 15:22).

problem: 2 (theology) — the note places the woman of Canaan under the spirits set over the nations and has Yahusha (Jesus) cross the line with mercy. She is seed scattered into that territory, not one of the nations; the bread is given to her because she is a child.
quote: The woman of Canaan comes from under one of those spirits, and her daughter is vexed with a devil to prove it. Yahusha (Jesus) names the line before he crosses it with mercy; the bread belongs to the household the Father rules directly.
fix: The woman on the coast of Canaan lives among the people under those spirits, and her daughter is vexed with a devil, but when she calls him *Son of David* and keeps asking, she shows she is not one of theirs. Yahusha (Jesus) says the bread is the children's, and then gives it to her, because she is a child of the household the Father rules directly, a lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered into the territory of the spirits (Matthew 15:24, 28).

problem: 2 (theology) — the note says outright that the woman of Canaan is not of the flock Yahusha (Jesus) was sent to, and that mercy crosses the line. The framework: she is of that flock, a daughter of the divorced house found in her scattering; the hearing revealed it.
quote: The woman of Canaan is not of that flock, and he tells her so. Then he feeds her anyway, at the crumbs, because the Father who rules Yashar'el (Israel) directly is also the one to whom all the nations belong. The line is kept, and mercy crosses it without erasing it.
fix: The woman on the coast of Canaan is of that flock, a daughter of the divorced northern house living in the land of her scattering, and the Shepherd who was sent only to the lost sheep found one of them there. He says the bread is for the children, she answers as a child who knows whose table it is, and he gives it to her (Matthew 15:28). The line is kept; she was on the inside of it all along, and the hearing revealed it.

problem: 2 (theology) — member note keeps the mercy-to-an-outsider reading.
quote: the children's bread is theirs, and mercy still reaches the crumbs (Matthew 15:26).
fix: the children's bread is theirs, and the woman on the coast of Canaan was one of the children (Matthew 15:26).

problem: 2 (theology) — the note says the woman of Canaan is not in the holy seed of Isaac and that Yahusha (Jesus) says so to her face, then feeds her outside the line. The framework reads her as that seed, revealed on the far side of her exile.
quote: The seed of promise has a name and a line, and the woman of Canaan is not in it, and Yahusha (Jesus) says so to her face. He does not lie to her to be kind; he keeps the line and then feeds her at it.
fix: The seed of promise has a name and a line, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not pretend otherwise; he tells her the bread is the children's. But he was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 15:24), and the coast of Tyre and Sidon was where the divorced northern house had been swallowed up among the Gentiles (Hosea 8:8). When she answers as one who knows the Master's table and he gives her the bread, he is not crossing the line; he is finding a child of Isaac's holy seed on the far side of her exile.

verdict: The rewrite is sound. Across all 126 notes the internal jargon of the old notes (wisdom-stream, substance, architecture, apparatus, Red Line, FRAMEWORK-MAJOR, hyphen-chains) is gone, the Come-and-See shape holds (both verses quoted in full with the citation after, then plain prose), book names are English throughout, sacred names carry their parentheticals outside quotations, son of man is rendered Son of Adam, and the prose reads as sentences rather than lists. The real connection of the old note survives in every card I checked, and in several the new note is more faithful to what the verses actually say than the old one was (the Matthew 12:12 Sabbath card, the Genesis 15:6 card, the Matthew 24:38 taken-and-left card, and the Matthew 28:19–20 commission cards are all squarely on the voice: Torah standing, grace as the way home to the commandments, the gathering of the scattered seed through all nations). Theology is clean with one exception, which is a cluster rather than a slip: the four Matthew 15 cards (4590–4593) and two of their member notes treat the woman of Canaan as an outsider to the seed who receives mercy at the edge of the line. That is the inherited reading, and the old notes carried it too, but the voice reads her as a lost sheep of the divorced northern house found in the land of her scattering, seed revealed by hearing, not a mercy case. The fixes above replace the closing sentences of those four cards and two member notes; nothing else needs touching. Minor stylistic items I left alone: the seven-baskets-as-jubilee reading in the Matthew 15:37 cards is a study-note inference, not an error, and 'the restored library' in the 2 Peter 3:6 card is readable to the app's reader.
